facts.text: Capping_Env builds a PyBullet simulation and a Panda robot with the gripper enabled, base position [-0.6, 0, 0], ee control and the Capping task
Capping_Env is registered as Capping{}{}-v1 in both control and reward variants, with max_episode_steps=100; the ee/sparse instance is Capping-v1
In ee control the Panda action space is Box(-1.0, 1.0) with four values: three displacement values and one gripper value (3 + 1 because the gripper is not blocked)
Panda.set_action clips the action to the action space low and high before using it
In ee control the first three action values are an end-effector displacement scaled by 0.05
The gripper action value is scaled by 0.2 and added to the current finger width
The Panda observation is seven values: end-effector position (3), end-effector velocity (3) and finger width (1)
The Capping task observation is nine values: cap base position (3), rotation (3) and velocity (3)
RobotTaskEnv._get_obs concatenates the robot and task observations and returns a dict with the keys observation, achieved_goal and desired_goal
The observation space is a Dict of three float32 Boxes bounded -200.0 to 200.0, for observation, desired_goal and achieved_goal; the action space is a Box(-1.0, 1.0) with the robot action shape
The achieved goal is six values: cap position (3) and end-effector position (3)
The desired goal is six values: cap target position (3) and vial end-effector position (3)
Capping.reset adds random xy offsets in [0, 0.05) to the cap and cap holder, to the vial and vial holder, and twice to the goal
The Capping task draws those placement offsets from Python's global random module, not from a seeded numpy generator
RobotTaskEnv.reset(seed) seeds the task's np_random generator, resets the robot and task, and returns the observation instead of an (observation, info) pair
The Capping task distance_threshold defaults to 0.015
is_success returns True when distance(achieved_goal, desired_goal) is below the task's distance_threshold
The reward is -1.2 while the cap touches the cap holder, otherwise -distance to the goal, and 1.0 when the task is already successful
RobotTaskEnv.step applies the robot action, advances the simulation, and returns (observation, reward, done, info) with done always False; success is only info['is_success']
The PyBullet wrapper defaults to 50 substeps, sets a 1/500 s physics timestep, gravity -9.81 m/s^2, and runs one physics step per substep
One PyBullet.step() therefore advances 50 * (1/500) = 0.1 s of simulated time, the control interval
The environment is simulated only: close() disconnects the PyBullet client and no hardware transport exists

determinism.notes: the package's fake seeds random.Random from reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1, so one seed and one action sequence give the same state hashes on the fake; upstream reset(seed) seeds the task's np_random generator but Capping.reset draws its offsets from Python's global random (Capping_Task.py:172-173), so the upstream path is not reproducible from the seed alone; neither path was compared with the other

gaps: the fake backend is a kinematic stand-in: it moves the end-effector and finger width and keeps the cap fixed, without PyBullet contact dynamics, collision response, mass, friction or the mesh scene, so it cannot reproduce the cap-holder contact reward or a physical insertion; the cap and goal are placeholders

the upstream physics timestep is 2 ms and one environment step runs 50 substeps (a 100 ms control interval, pybullet.py:25-54); the fake advances one placeholder kinematic step per tick and does not integrate physics, so it does not model that interval

the fake follows the old Gym API of the upstream class (reset returns an observation, step a four-tuple with done always False) and applies the registration's 100-step limit through done, so the bridge reports the 100th tick as terminated rather than truncated
no wall-clock pacing (realtime_factor 0); the fake was not compared with the upstream PyBullet environment, and the model was never validated against a physical Panda or a laboratory task
snapshot and restore are not offered: the environment exposes save_state/restore_state over PyBullet but no get_state/set_state that the bridge requires, so cap.world.snapshot.v1 is not bound
rendering (human or rgb_array at 720 x 480, core.py:303-343) is not exposed by the cap.world.* classes

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
